mutation_aliasing: The input matrix, entries and row links are never modified. On incompatible dimensions, the returned object intentionally aliases mat and all its original rows, so later caller writes through that result affect the input. On compatible dimensions, every output row is fresh and distinct from all input rows and other output rows; values are immutable integers. No private mutable state persists between calls.

The compatible branch uses separate output row/column cursors instead of dividing a large flattened index, avoiding rounding near integer-division boundaries. Every cursor is an exact integer; the final output_row increment reaches r only after the final write, and no out-of-range access follows.

Compatible reshaping takes O(m*n + r + 1) time including zero initialization and O(1) auxiliary state excluding O(r*c + r + 1) output storage. Every row is separately allocated. No intermediate flat copy is built.
